STOP mid-run if: a captured frame holds fewer than 50 distinct colours (a near-uniform frame is what a broken capture produces, not evidence the app drew nothing); a frame is UNCHANGED after a click or after submit (the step did not take, and typing into a screen that is not the form would produce a confident wrong frame); no refusal box is found at the declared colour; the app's log does not show the loopback proxy intercepting https://assistant.skipi.app/; or either typed credential appears in a log this stage publishes. A FAILED BIND IS NOT A STOP: if the 503 proxy cannot take 19166 the driver records a FINDING and retries on 19167, and only the loss of both ports stops the stage. An instrument that dies of a busy address loses a stage to weather.

The rendered colour is measured two ways because they answer different questions: contrast_core (darkest glyph pixel against the modal background) asks whether the DECLARED colour landed and returns 6.40 exactly; contrast_mean averages every glyph pixel including antialiased edges and returns about 5.55. smoke-3d's README recorded 6.09/5.94, which is a THIRD estimator over a different glyph population - not a disagreement to reconcile, and not a confirmation either. streams.why_only_S1_and_why_that_is_not_a_reduct: Three borders, each measured on this commit and on the built binary, and the second one closes the obvious workaround. (1) ACCOUNT_ORIGIN is a compile-time const (native_account.rs:7) and the dev override is option_env! (:382) - the COMPILER's environment, so a running app cannot be redirected. (2) That branch and the direct_loopback_qa field it reads are both #[cfg(debug_assertions)] (:381, :385-386), so the branch does not exist in a release build at all: rebuilding the RELEASE profile with the variable set still yields the production origin. (3) The account client is reqwest 0.12.28 with feature rustls-tls, which reqwest's own Cargo.toml:148 defines as rustls-tls-webpki-roots - bundled Mozilla roots, no runtime path to add a certificate. So S2/S3/S4 each need a completed TLS session to a domain we do not own, signed by a public CA; we do not obtain one and we do not stand up our own CA (manager, 05.11, as a prohibition rather than an observation). S1 needs no TLS - only a failed connection - and is therefore the one state this binary can show honestly. The loopback stand being debug-only is a SECURITY BOUNDARY the product states in its own comment, so DEBUG is not a weaker profile here; it is the only instrument that reaches the other three.
streams.a_correction_to_my_own_stated_cause_that: I first attributed the SSL_CERT_FILE string in the binary to reqwest 0.13.2 and rustls-platform-verifier. He measured 0 occurrences in all three crates I named: the string comes from openssl-probe 0.2.1, reached via rustls-native-certs 0.8.3 via rustls-platform-verifier via reqwest 0.13.2 - the UPDATER's client. I verified both halves myself rather than adopting them: reqwest 0.12.28/src holds 0 occurrences, and its Cargo.toml:148 reads rustls-tls = ["rustls-tls-webpki-roots"]. The conclusion survived and the stated cause did not. The form matters more than the fix: a correct conclusion carried on a non-existent mechanism would have gone into the acceptance record as a reason any reader could refute with one grep - and had the Cargo.toml said rustls-tls-native-roots instead, the conclusion itself would have been FALSE.

streams.the_instrument_was_calibrated_before_thi: smoke-tool.py was run against the existing smoke-3d frames before being pinned here, on the principle that an instrument should be aimed at a known object before it is aimed at an unknown one. Two faults surfaced that would otherwise have reached the stage. First, its text extractor returned a confident ZERO for all four RU keys: the language-table opener `ru: {` sits at indent 2 while `en: {` sits at indent 4, and there are four `en:` tables in the file, so a regex pinned to one indentation found English and silently missed Russian. It now attributes each key occurrence to the nearest opener above it rather than slicing 'the' table. Second, its unescaping went through `.encode().decode('unicode_escape')`, which routes UTF-8 through latin-1 and turned every em-dash into mojibake; it now uses json.loads. A third fault was cosmetic but worth naming: the line counter at gap 6 reported the two-line second-step boxes as one line, which is why box HEIGHT and not line count is the discriminator this stage relies on.
streams.what_the_app_log_proves_and_why_it_outra: The rehearsal found, rather than the design anticipating, that reqwest logs at TRACE and the binary therefore states its own case: `proxy(http://127.0.0.1:19165/) intercepts 'https://assistant.skipi.app/'`. That single line proves at RUNTIME what the source said at compile time - this release binary's account origin IS production - and simultaneously proves the request went to the loopback proxy instead of to the real host. Geometry says a refusal was drawn; the log says which host was asked and that nothing reached it. The driver requires that line in every run. The same log was also checked for both typed credentials and held neither (measured: 0 occurrences of each, in a 1405-byte log), which matters because these files are published to a person rather than merely stored.
streams.why_the_ports_sit_below_the_ephemeral_ra: The coordinator's required correction, re-measured by me before adopting it. My first choice, 19165/19166, sat INSIDE the kernel's ephemeral range: /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range is 32768-60999, ip_local_reserved_ports is EMPTY, and 166 sockets occupy that range right now. Two distinct consequences, and only the second is about my own port. (1) The bind on the proxy port could fail with EADDRINUSE through nobody's fault, and my STOP list had no entry for a failed bind, so it would have surfaced as some other error. (2) The 'closed port' claim is a point measurement of a MOVING property - the kernel can hand that number to any process as an outgoing port mid-stage. Declaring the port in `reads` reserves nothing, and even `writes` only excludes DECLARED neighbours while the hazard here is an unnamed system process - so the declaration is not the cure and the choice of port is. 19165/19166/19167 are below 32768, which the kernel never hands out; all three measured free. The port predicate is now ONE shell function called both in the preconditions and before every run, because two copies of a predicate drift and the copy that drifts is the one nobody re-reads.
streams.why_this_is_a_fresh_step_1_and_not_a_ste: The coordinator asked for step 3 after three required edits. The edits themselves make step 3 structurally impossible, and his own generator says so: with CREWING_REQUEST_REPO set correctly, `build-request.py step3` refuses on exactly six paths - card_provenance.sha256_file (removed), card_provenance.sha256_file_at_read and read_at (added), driver.sha256 and evidence_files[0].sha256 (the driver, changed by the port fix and the bind-retry), and evidence_files[1].sha256 (smoke-tool.py, changed by the bind exit code). Step 3 may differ from the reviewed step 1 only in event_id, heartbeat, heartbeat_note and submission. So this is a fresh review-only bundle: the reviewed bytes changed because the reviewer required them to change, and re-review is what the rule is for. A first attempt also moved repo/head/status/untracked because I ran the generator without CREWING_REQUEST_REPO - the same implicit-input trap already recorded in my notes, caught by the generator rather than by me.
